question: Should OpenClaw accept `{ owner }` records as the current persisted plugin-slot config contract, and if so should this stale draft be refreshed or replaced by a narrower implementation?
rationale: The code direction changes a public config/API shape and touches auth/startup availability; automation can identify defects but cannot decide whether this contract should be accepted now.

options.title: Request a refreshed branch
options.body: Ask the contributor to rebase, fix the remaining blockers, and add redacted exact-head terminal/log proof before another merge review.

options.title: Sponsor a replacement implementation
options.body: Have a maintainer or repair lane recreate the owner-record support narrowly from current main while preserving contributor credit and linked context.

options.title: Pause the contract
options.body: Keep or later close the PR if maintainers are not ready to accept object-form plugin-slot records as a supported config shape.

recommendation.title: Request a refreshed branch
recommendation.body: Ask the contributor to rebase, fix the remaining blockers, and add redacted exact-head terminal/log proof before another merge review.

likelyOwner.reason: The branch touches provider auth trust and config compatibility surfaces where Peter Steinberger has recent feature history, and the decision is broader than slot helper mechanics alone.
